title: The Voynich manuscript may be bound in the wrong order
excerpt: Researchers propose that the Voynich manuscript was bound in the wrong order. Cut illustrations, changes in handwriting and statistical analysis support the hypothesis published in Digital Medievalist.
content:
Researchers Colin Layfield, from the University of Malta, and Lisa Fagin Davis have published a hypothesis about the Voynich manuscript in Digital Medievalist: its pages may have been bound in a different order than the original. The illustrations that are interrupted at the edges and continue on distant pages, the alternation of scripts, and the statistical analysis of the text support this idea.

Statistical analysis of the text as a tool for reordering the pages 📊

The study relies on statistical analysis of the text to detect patterns that do not fit the current sequence. The alternation of scripts throughout the volume suggests that leaves with different features were interleaved after binding. Added to this are the illustrations cut off at the edges that continue on pages far apart from each other. The parchment dates from between 1404 and 1438, and the work remains undeciphered. The conclusion is that studies based on the current order of the pages should be reviewed.

Centuries spent searching for the meaning, and perhaps all that was needed was to reorder the leaves 📚

After decades of cryptographers, linguists, and enthusiasts racking their brains over the text, it turns out that part of the mystery might be solved by something akin to reshuffling the pages. In other words, the world's most enigmatic book may simply have been badly bound. Previous studies will need to be reviewed, although some researchers will already be thinking about asking the bookbinder for a second opinion.
